tasks.title: Decide the fate of resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain — no production callers remain
tasks.description: Task #51 deleted warnIfLegacyApiKey and its two call sites (src/commands/narrate.ts, src/commands/run.ts), which were the only consumers of resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain(). The function is still exported from src/config.ts and covered by test/config.test.ts, but nothing in src/ calls it — the resolution is now purely documentary, mirroring the same chain in lib/cairn_narrate_server.py (see task #59). Either (a) delete the helper, its AnthropicApiKeyResolution type, and its tests, leaving the Python server as the single implementation, or (b) keep it and give it a real caller — e.g. have runNarrate/runRun pass the resolved key into the narration server env instead of relying on the child process re-reading the environment. Do NOT normalize onto plain ANTHROPIC_API_KEY under either option: the loop deliberately blanks that name to force Max-plan usage. Sequence this after #59 so both sides of the mirror are decided together.
tasks.notes:
# Task #66 — Fate of `resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain`

## Decision: option (a) — deleted the helper

The task offered two options. I chose deletion. The reasoning, so a future agent
doesn't re-litigate it:

1. **Option (b) has no behavioral effect.** The premise of (b) was "pass the resolved
   key into the narration server env instead of relying on the child re-reading the
   environment." But `startNarrationServer()` (`src/narration.ts:80`) spawns the Python
   server with `{ detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' }` and **no `env` option**, so the
   child inherits the parent's `process.env` verbatim. Critically, the
   `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` blanking is *per-spawn and non-mutating* — every site builds a
   fresh object (`{ ...process.env, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: '' }` at `run.ts:205`,
   `plan.ts:170`, `summarize.ts:111`, `post-task-reviewer.ts:119`). The parent's own
   `process.env` is never touched. So the narration server already sees the real key
   under whichever name the user exported. Threading a TS-resolved value through would
   have been pure ceremony.
2. **Option (b) can't collapse the mirror either.** `lib/cairn_narrate_server.py` is a
   standalone `argparse` script — it can be launched directly, not just via
   `startNarrationServer`. It must therefore keep its own resolution chain regardless.
   Option (b) would have left us with two implementations *plus* new env plumbing;
   option (a) leaves exactly one, sited where the key is actually consumed.

## Changes

- **`src/config.ts`** — deleted the `AnthropicApiKeyResolution` interface, the
  `resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain()` function, and its doc comment (was lines 155–179).
  `setConfigEnvVars()` is now the last export in the file.
- **`test/config.test.ts`** — deleted the 6-test `describe('resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain')`
  block and dropped the symbol from the top-level import.
- **`lib/cairn_narrate_server.py`** (~line 224) — the comment above the key resolution
  ended with "Mirrors `resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain()` in `src/config.ts`", which this
  task turned into a dangling reference. Rewrote it to (a) state plainly that this is
  now the *only* implementation and the TypeScript side deliberately has none, and
  (b) absorb the "never normalize the resolved value back onto `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`"
  invariant that was documented only in the deleted TS docstring. That invariant is
  non-obvious and load-bearing (it's what preserves Max-plan forcing), so it needed a
  new home rather than being deleted with its old one.
- **`src/commands/narrate.ts`, `src/commands/run.ts`** — listed in the task's `files`
  but required **no change**. Task #51 had already removed `warnIfLegacyApiKey` and both
  call sites; neither file imports from `../config` at all today. Verified, not assumed.

## Verification

- `grep -rn "resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain\|AnthropicApiKeyResolution" src test lib docs
  README.md CLAUDE.md` → **zero hits** (exit 1). No dangling references anywhere,
  including prose.
- `bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck` → clean,
  108 modules bundled. **Run from the project root** — see the caveat below.
- `bun test` → **799 pass, 0 fail, 29 files**. Baseline from task #65 was 805; we
  removed exactly 6 tests, so 805 − 6 = 799. Exact match, no collateral breakage.
- Did **not** modify `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck` and did **not** run `./install.sh`,
  per the pin/unpin procedure.

## Important: the "BUILD HEALTH CHECK FAILED" banner this iteration was a FALSE ALARM

This iteration's prompt opened with `FileNotFound opening root directory "src"`. The
build is **green** — the failure is a cairn bug, not a codebase error.

`src/health-check.ts:55` computes `cwd = taskDir ? join(projectRoot, taskDir)
: projectRoot` and runs the project-wide `healthCheck` string there. Task #66's
`directory` is `src`, so the health check ran from `<root>/src`, where the
root-relative path `src/index.ts` doesn't exist. The identical command from the
project root succeeds (verified above).

Filed as **discovered task #68** (`src/health-check.ts`, `test/health-check.test.ts`)
with a recommended fix of always running the health check from `projectRoot`, and a
note that `shouldRunHealthCheck()`'s `join(cwd, 'package.json')` probe carries the same
cwd assumption and should be fixed in the same pass. Payload file left at
`.cairn/.discovered-66.json` — safe to delete.

Note for whoever picks up #68: `cairn task add --file` requires the JSON payload to be
a **single object**, not an array. An array fails with
`validation failed — (root): must be object`.

## Remaining work

After this task, `tasks.json` still has discovered task **#68** pending, so
`.cairn_complete` was **not** created.

tasks.title: Health check runs from the task directory, so root-relative healthCheck commands fail spuriously
tasks.description: src/health-check.ts:55 computes `cwd = taskDir ? join(projectRoot, taskDir) : projectRoot` and runs the project-level `healthCheck` command there. But `healthCheck` is a single project-wide string in cairn.json, written relative to the project root — cairn's own is `bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck`. For any task whose `directory` field is not the project root, that command is executed from `<root>/<directory>` and fails on paths that resolve fine from the root. Observed live in iteration 16: task #66 has `directory: "src"`, so the pre-iteration health check ran from `<root>/src`, where `src/index.ts` does not exist, and the agent was handed a `BUILD HEALTH CHECK FAILED: FileNotFound opening root directory "src"` banner describing a build that is actually green (verified: the same command from the project root succeeds). This is a false failure signal on every non-root task and wastes agent attention chasing a nonexistent break. Decide and implement one of: (a) always run `healthCheck` from `projectRoot` and drop the `taskDir` join — simplest, matches the fact that the command is project-wide; (b) keep the per-directory cwd but make it opt-in via a per-directory health check config. Prefer (a) unless there is a known consumer relying on per-directory cwd. Note that `shouldRunHealthCheck()` also probes `join(cwd, 'package.json')` for the `npm run type-check` special case and has the same cwd assumption — fix both together. Update test/health-check.test.ts to cover a non-root taskDir with a root-relative command.
